facts.evaporation: A large city tree can evaporate up to 400 liters of water a day, cooling its surroundings by up to 3°C.
facts.oxygen: A single beech tree produces enough oxygen for 10 people per year.
facts.dust: City trees filter a significant share of particulate matter from the air in their immediate surroundings.
facts.roots: The roots of a street tree often extend over one and a half times the area of its crown.
facts.co2: Over its lifetime, a 100-year-old tree has bound around 5 tons of CO₂.
facts.network: Trees communicate through underground fungal networks, known as the “Wood Wide Web”.
facts.lifespan: Street trees live an average of only 60 years. In rural areas, they live three times as long.
facts.noise: A dense stand of trees can reduce noise levels by up to 10 decibels.
facts.water: In hot summers, a city tree needs up to 200 additional liters of water per week.

introduction.title: Measure. Understand. Act.
introduction.description: Green Ecolution combines three steps into one platform. Sensors measure what is happening on site, the software turns that into a situation overview, and operations planning converts it into tours. We started with the irrigation of urban trees, and the platform is designed for further tasks.

measure.label: Measure
measure.description: Sensors deliver measurements from the city, for irrigation the soil moisture at variable depths.

understand.label: Understand
understand.description: The platform analyses the measurement series and shows on a map and dashboard where action is needed.

act.label: Act
act.description: Operations and route planning turns the situation overview into tours that avoid unnecessary journeys.

extend.label: Modularly extensible
extend.description: Further sensor types and use cases can be connected with some development work. Irrigation is the first.

challenge.supportingText: Urban green spaces regulate the microclimate, promote biodiversity and strengthen a location's competitiveness. But persistent drought and a lack of digitalization threaten this asset. Many municipalities base their irrigation planning solely on the judgment of individual staff, with no data basis at all. Instead of demand-based irrigation, watering is done uniformly, wasting water while still not reaching every tree. Unoptimized irrigation trips also cause avoidable CO₂ emissions.

waterUse.description: Water is consumed by a mid-sized municipality for irrigation, often without a data basis and without demand-based control.

treeCost.description: is the cost of a single street tree. If it is lost due to insufficient irrigation, this damage alone covers the sensor costs for several years.

bedCost.description: can be the cost of a complete street bed, including civil works, substrate and infrastructure.

targetGroups.title: Who benefits
targetGroups.description: Green Ecolution is built for municipal operations. The benefit differs depending on the role.

municipality.description: Decisions about water, staff and vehicles rest on measurements instead of experience. Consumption and operations are documented per area and per tour, and can therefore be evidenced.

operations.description: Schedules and tours are generated instead of assembled by hand. The fleet, the teams and the review of actual consumption all live in one place.

field.description: The tour can be viewed in the app and can also be transferred to the navigation device in the vehicle. A traffic-light system on the map shows which trees and groups need water.

it.description: We run the platform, and where preferred inside the municipality's own Kubernetes cluster. Open interfaces, a plug-in system and open source keep the data and the control in house.

targetGroups.closing: Everyone else benefits indirectly: healthy urban trees cool the city climate and support biodiversity.

sensorProbe.illustrationAriaLabel: Schematic diagram of a soil probe measuring at several depths
sensorProbe.title: The soil probe
sensorProbe.description: Designed for use in public spaces. The probe measures at variable depths and so maps the root profile of a tree, from the near-surface fine roots to the deeper main roots. This makes it possible to see whether water actually reaches the root zone or only wets the surface. Installation is flush with the ground using standard soil augers, and maintenance work such as mowing is not affected.
sensorProbe.probeCarrier: The probe is one possible sensor, not the only one. The platform is built so that other sensors can be connected as well with some development work.
sensorProbe.availability: You get the probes directly from us, and your team can install them itself.

workflow.title: The end-to-end workflow

measure.title: Measure
measure.description: Soil moisture sensors capture soil moisture and temperature at variable depths. The data is transmitted energy-efficiently via LoRaWAN.

understand.title: Understand
understand.description: A traffic-light system shows the current irrigation need on a map. Staff can see at a glance which green spaces need water. Time series enable detailed analyses.

act.title: Act
act.description: Automated dispatch and route planning generates optimized irrigation routes, taking into account water capacity, vehicle size, and road restrictions.

workflow.photoLead: In the end it comes down to the run. The route is settled before the vehicle leaves: which sites need water, how much has to be carried and in what order they are visited. Instead of a blanket round, it follows what the sensors in the ground have measured.
workflow.photoAlt: A worker from the municipal service centre waters a young tree supported by a wooden frame, using a hose.
workflow.photoCaption: Watering by the municipal service centre of Flensburg.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about Green Ecolution

origin.question: Who is behind Green Ecolution?
origin.answerPlain:
Green Ecolution is a company based in Flensburg. {{director}} founded it together with {{group}} and runs it as managing director.

It began with a question from the City of Flensburg, which turned to Smarte Grenzregion with it. That became a master's project in Applied Computer Science at Flensburg University of Applied Sciences, together with the municipal service centre of Flensburg. In user tests with the service centre the application scored an above-average usability rating and was described as clear and manageable even by staff without an IT background.

We founded the company so that municipalities can use the solution in their daily work. You can find more on the About us page.

value.question: What value does Green Ecolution provide?
value.answerPlain:
Green Ecolution makes the watering of urban trees traceable. Sensor data shows which areas need water, and the scheduling turns that into tours without unnecessary trips. Watering this deliberately saves water, fuel and staff time, and decisions rest on measurements instead of experience.

For municipalities that means missing water becomes visible earlier, consumption is documented, and the solution can be operated in-house and developed further together, without being tied to a single vendor.

requirements.question: What does a municipality need to bring?
requirements.answerPlain:
For scheduling and route planning, the locations of the trees and areas, the vehicles you already have with their water capacities and the refill points across the city are enough. Sensors are not a prerequisite for this; they improve the prioritisation. Once probes are added they need a radio link: LoRaWAN today, or NB-IoT with a SIM card as an alternative.

Which data and which infrastructure are needed in detail is set out under the requirements on the product page.

openSource.question: What does the open source code give us?
openSource.answerPlain:
Three things, in practical terms. You can read and have audited what the system does with your data. There are no licence fees. And you are not tied to a vendor: the source code is public on GitHub and stays with the municipality even if it decides differently later.

Setup, operation and support are ours to handle. Open means you could do it yourself, not that you have to.

sensors.question: Is the system tied to specific sensors?
sensors.answerPlain:
No. The platform is modular, and our soil probe is one possible sensor, not the only one. Sensors from other manufacturers can be connected through The Things Network and the plug-in system. A new sensor type needs some development work, which we take care of. Connecting third-party sensors has not been proven in the field so far.

The soil probe we supply is built for public spaces and measures at variable depths. In the research project it contained a Watermark sensor for soil water tension and an SMT100 sensor for soil moisture and temperature. Today a series-produced model sits in the ground instead of the research prototype.

cost.question: What does it cost to use?
cost.answerPlain:
The software itself costs nothing; it is open source and free of licence fees. You pay for the probes, which you buy once, for the setup and, if we operate the platform for you, for the ongoing operation.

How this adds up is set out in the pricing model on the services page. We prepare a specific quote after an initial conversation.
